It is fine if the answer also notes an indirect/transitive chain (drawer → singleFolderMode → visibility argument) as long as it still denies a direct use by setVisibility.

Deduct 2 points: If the answer does not make that explicit pairing—e.g., it only gives a global statement about drawer usage such as “drawer is only used in the null check” or “drawer is not read anywhere after the guard” without naming setVisibility; or it merely describes what the setVisibility argument is derived from (e.g., “visibility is set from singleFolderMode / View.VISIBLE vs GONE”) without explicitly stating that setVisibility does not use/read drawer.

Deduct 3 points only if the answer claims a data/value-level use of drawer at the actionBarSubTitle.setVisibility call site — that is, it asserts that drawer (or a value read from drawer) is the receiver, an argument, or otherwise flows into the setVisibility statement.

Do not deduct when the answer merely describes control-flow/reachability (e.g., “the call is inside the if (drawer != null) block,” “it executes only when drawer is non-null”), since that is not a value-level usage. Also do not deduct if the answer describes a transitive relationship via an intermediate such as singleFolderMode, so long as it does not say that drawer itself appears in or is read by the setVisibility statement.

Deduct 2 points only if the answer is silent about how singleFolderMode relates to drawer—i.e., it makes no statement or description that connects singleFolderMode to drawer at all.

Do not deduct if the answer addresses their relationship in any way, whether explicitly or implicitly. It does not need to use the words “depends on.” For example, no deduction if the answer:
- Notes that singleFolderMode is assigned inside an if (drawer != null) block, or that its assignment is reached only when drawer is non-null.
- Explicitly states there is (or is not) a data dependency between singleFolderMode and drawer.

Deduct 2 points only if the answer does not specifically link the drawer null-check to the reachability of actionBarSubTitle.setVisibility. To avoid deduction, the answer must either:
- Explicitly state in prose that the call to actionBarSubTitle.setVisibility is only reached/executed when drawer != null, or
- Reproduce or cite the relevant code (e.g., if (drawer != null) { ... actionBarSubTitle.setVisibility(...) ... }) or point to the lines showing that setVisibility sits inside the null-guard. Quoting/citing the code alone counts; no extra explanation is required.

Generic remarks that drawer may be null, that there is a null check, or that some code is guarded do not suffice unless they name actionBarSubTitle.setVisibility (or the specific statement/block containing it) as the code whose execution depends on drawer being non-null.
